title: Per-endpoint intent-aware SLI taxonomy, error-budget mediation, and coordinated circuit-breaker bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a concrete, implementable taxonomy and policy for extracting intent-aware SLIs per model endpoint, mediate error-budget transfers across regions/variants, and bind those SLOs to per-route circuit-breakers and prioritized load-shedding. This ticket covers design decisions, SLI extraction rules, error-budget accounting primitives, and the policy surface that will be enforced by the routing/circuit-breaker service.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published SLI taxonomy doc in Confluence with examples for text-generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking routes. 2) A JSON SLI manifest schema implemented in the runtime for per-endpoint SLI config. 3) Error-budget mediation algorithm prototype (simulator + test harness) that demonstrates cross-region transfer and weighted borrowing. 4) Circuit-breaker bindings implemented as policy objects and validated by chaos tests showing graceful degradations under targeted overloads. 5) Updated Console SLO dashboard to show per-endpoint error budget status and transfer events.
design_notes:
High-level approach:
  - Intent-aware SLI extraction: Tag incoming requests with 'intent' derived from route + prompt metadata (examples: interactive-chat, batch-embed, high-confidence-rerank). For each intent, define a primary SLI (availability, quality, or latency) and a backup SLI for fallback signals.
  - SLI examples: availability = 200 responses / 500ms for low-latency routes; quality = top-1 semantic similarity >= 0.82 for embeddings/rerank; conversational coherence measured with reference promptset autometrics for chat.
  - Signal composition rules: For structured outputs (tool-calling / function responses), compute a hierarchical SLI: success of schema validation -> semantic correctness -> latency. SLI failure at any critical node marks the request as failed for error-budget accounting.
  - Error-budget mediation: Maintain per-endpoint + per-region budgets; allow temporary crediting between regions subject to a capped transfer rate and a reconciliation window. Prioritize transfers that preserve high-priority tenants' budgets.
  - Circuit-breaker bindings: Define policy objects with filters (route, model-variant, priority, intent). Each policy maps SLO thresholds -> CB thresholds (open at 2x burn rate over 5m, half-open after cooldown). CBs can apply soft-degradation (quantization, lower-context variant) before hard-dropping.
  - Load-shedding order: (1) best-effort non-critical batch work, (2) low-priority tenants, (3) degraded model variants, (4) hard rejection. Eviction credits and grace quotas are tracked in a ledger.
tradeoffs_considered:
- Simplicity vs expressivity: A simple per-route boolean SLI is easy to enforce but misses quality nuances; intent tagging adds complexity but enables fairer load-shedding.
- Centralized vs distributed budgeting: Centralized accounting simplifies mediation but adds latency and single-point-of-failure; hybrid local-first with periodic reconciliation chosen.
- Soft degradation vs immediate failover: Soft degradation preserves availability but risks quality regressions; default to graded fallbacks with safe-guards (promptset evals) enabled.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft SLI taxonomy and canonical examples; implement SLI manifest schema in repo (config path: services/routing/sli-manifests/). Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement local SLI counters and burn-rate computation in edge agents; build simulator and run synthetic traffic. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Implement cross-region mediation and ledger; integrate with circuit-breaker service to accept policy objects. Phase 4 (1 week): Canary rollout to non-critical routes and runtime chaos testing. Phase 5: Console updates + docs + runbook.
risks:
- Incorrect intent classification could misattribute failures. Mitigation: conservative default intent and audit logs.
- Transfer loops between regions causing oscillation. Mitigation: transfer cap and backoff hysteresis.
- Console shows stale budget state during reconciliation. Mitigation: show last-updated timestamp and reconciliation status.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: SLI manifest parser and counter semantics.
- Simulator tests: synthetic workloads representing chat/embeddings/rerank with configurable failure modes.
- Integration: connect ledger to CB service and run fail-open / fail-closed scenarios in staging.
- Chaos: introduce region-level capacity drops and verify prioritized shedding meets policy objectives.
rollout_notes: Canary on non-customer-critical routes (internal tools / sandbox tenants) for 72 hours. Observe burn-rate signals and CB activations. If quality regressions detected, auto-revert policy via runtime feature-flag. Notify SRE and Solutions Eng teams 24h before canary.
